# 0001: Draw sprites as inline SVG generated by Python

- Status: accepted
- Date: 2026-11-13
- Round: 2 (requirements R2, R3, R4)

## Y-statement

In the context of **adding player and opponent sprites to Math Quest (R2–R4)**,
facing **the rules that the program is Python-only, needs nothing installed, and keeps
every page generated inside `web.py` with no separate asset files**,
we decided for **drawing each sprite as SVG shapes stored as Python strings in
`sprites.py` and placed directly ("inline") into the HTML**
and neglected **PNG image files served by the server, emoji characters, and ASCII art**,
to achieve **pictures that match each opponent's name, scale to any size without going
blurry, stay testable with plain string checks, and need no new files, routes, or
packages**,
accepting that **the drawings are simple geometric shapes rather than detailed pixel
art, and that adding a new character means writing SVG by hand**.

## Alternatives considered

| Option | Why not chosen |
|---|---|
| PNG image files in an `images/` folder | Needs image files (not Python), a new route in `web.py` to serve them, and someone to draw them. |
| Emoji (🐉 🧙) | Very little code, but there is no slime, goblin or troll emoji, so R4 could not be met. Emoji also look different on every device. |
| ASCII art in a `<pre>` block | Python-only, but hard to read at small sizes and much less fun to look at. |

## Consequences

- `Opponent.sprite` names a key in `sprites.MONSTERS`. A test (R4) checks that this key
  matches the first word of the opponent's name.
- An opponent with no sprite gets a grey "?" placeholder instead of crashing the page.
- The page now uses the CSS `:has()` selector to highlight the chosen hero. Very old
  browsers will still work, but won't show the highlight.
